name: Massachusetts
scope: Alimony after divorce under the Alimony Reform Act (M.G.L. c. 208, §§ 48-55): general term, rehabilitative, reimbursement and transitional alimony; duration limits apply to general term alimony.

formula.text: Except for reimbursement alimony or unusual circumstances, alimony should generally not exceed the recipient's need or 30-35% of the difference between the parties' gross incomes when the order issues (M.G.L. c. 208, § 53(b), as explained by the Probate and Family Court). Gross income is the Child Support Guidelines definition, excluding capital gains, dividends and interest from assets already divided, and income already used for a child support order. The new spouse's income of a remarried payer is not considered.

duration.text: General term alimony maximum (M.G.L. c. 208, § 49(b), per the Probate and Family Court): marriages of 5 years or less: 50% of the number of months married; 10 years or less: 60%; 15 years or less: 70%; 20 years or less: 80%; more than 20 years: as long as the judge finds fair. Alimony normally ends on the death of either spouse, remarriage of the recipient, or the payer reaching full retirement age; cohabitation for at least 3 months can reduce or end it.

eligibility.text: Alimony is paid by a spouse able to pay to a spouse in need; the court weighs length of marriage, age, health, income and employability, economic and non-economic contributions, marital lifestyle, ability to maintain it, lost economic opportunity and other factors. Reimbursement and transitional alimony are only for marriages of no more than 5 years.

taxNote.text: Federal: for divorce or separation agreements executed after 2018 (or older ones modified to adopt the new rule), the payer cannot deduct alimony and the recipient does not include it in gross income (IRS Topic No. 452).

testCases.what: monthly general term alimony ceiling range (30%-35% of the gross difference), 12 years: 70% of 144 months
testCases.source: computed by hand from M.G.L. c. 208 §§ 49(b), 53(b) as stated by the Probate and Family Court

testCases.what: monthly range 30%-35% of 4,000; 60-month marriage: 30 months (court's example)
testCases.source: computed by hand from M.G.L. c. 208 §§ 49(b), 53(b) as stated by the Probate and Family Court

facts.text: General term alimony normally stops when the payer reaches full retirement age, unless the judge orders otherwise.
Living with a partner for at least 3 months can reduce or end the recipient's alimony.
Reimbursement and transitional alimony are reserved to marriages of no more than 5 years.
When a remarried payer's alimony is reviewed for an increase, the new spouse's income is not considered.
